The claim intent-command-deployment-evidence has stood planned with no responsibility (docs/CLAIMS.yaml:961-968), and the intent-satisfaction milestone declares command and deployment evidence non-scope (branch feature/satisfaction-is-explained). The parts exist: `majordomus served observe` fetches a deployment's build identity, judges it against a commit by containment and records the observation (apps/majordomus-cli/src/served.rs:15-35, 646-675, test/cases/384_a_deployment_is_evidence.sh), and every ledger execution already carries the command that produced it (apps/majordomus-cli/src/evidence/mod.rs:<n1/>). en: <t1/> measures the Rust executable's coverage once — one instrumented export, test code excluded from both the covered and the total so a test added never flatters the number — and reports line, function and region coverage by one rule. Three gates read that one judgment. The crate floor (<t2/>) is a lower bound on the whole executable. The session/continuity domain (<t3/>) is held to a floor of its own on lines, functions and regions. Both floors are ratchets: each is the coverage its subject measured when it was set, and may rise and never fall. And the differential gate (<t4/>, rule <t5/>) holds every executable line, function and region a change adds or touches — measured against the branch's merge-base with the trunk, working tree included — so a change that introduces uncovered code is refused even while the aggregate percentage barely moves.

en: Every server restart is a new stream of the journal, so runtimes compact away streams that have been dead for long. Compaction takes away the records of those streams and nothing anyone still relies on: a claim that holds and a session that is open are never touched; a handover nobody has taken keeps its stream for a day past the retention, and no longer, so a machine whose runs each handed over something cannot fill its quota with the dead; a handover still offered keeps everyone who took it, and a review keeps every answer, even when the taker's or the answerer's runtime has stopped. And a runtime compacted away while it slept — a laptop past the expiry and the fifteen-minute retention — is heard again when it wakes: its peers fetch its stream again from the first event, so a claim it took before it slept holds again there and refuses a conflicting one.
cs: Každý restart serveru je nový stream žurnálu, takže runtime kompaktují streamy, které jsou dlouho mrtvé. Compaction odebírá záznamy těchto streamů a nic, na co se ještě někdo spoléhá: platný nárok a otevřená relace se nikdy nedotknou; předávka, kterou nikdo nevzal, drží svůj stream den po retenci a ne déle, takže stroj, jehož každý běh něco předal, nemůže zaplnit kvótu mrtvými; stále nabízená předávka drží každého, kdo ji vzal, a revize drží každou odpověď, i když runtime toho, kdo vzal nebo odpověděl, přestal běžet. A runtime zkompaktovaný, zatímco spal — notebook po expiraci a patnáctiminutové retenci — je opět slyšet, když se probudí: jeho peery znovu stáhnou jeho stream od první události, takže nárok, který převzal před spánkem, tam opět platí a odmítne konfliktní.

en: <t1/> is the committed projection, written by <t2/> and checked by <t3/>. It exists because the site generator runs without a Rust toolchain and reads committed artifacts; the Rust resolution is authoritative and the file is never edited by hand. It omits <t4/>, which is a fact of one checkout's artifacts and would make every clone report drift; the documentation and the rustdoc are declared by discovery rather than by their output, so the file is byte-identical whether or not either producer ran, and <t5/> holds it so. A report is the other kind of surface: known only from the <t6/> its producer wrote, it exists in the checkout that ran the producer and in no other, so the file leaves it out while the process that finds it still serves and composes it (<t7/>). A surface meant to be in the committed file — to be published by the site build on every machine — is declared by discovery from what says it exists, as the rustdoc is from the crate.

Vynechává <t4/>, což je fakt artefaktů jednoho checkoutu a způsobilo by, že každý klon hlásí drift; dokumentace a rustdoc jsou deklarovány discovery, nikoli podle svého výstupu, takže je soubor bajt po bajtu identický bez ohledu na to, zda některý producent běžel, a <t5/> to drží. Report je druhý druh povrchu: známý jen z <t6/>, který zapsal jeho producent, existuje v checkoutu, který producenta spustil, a v žádném jiném, takže jej soubor vynechává, zatímco proces, který jej najde, jej stále obsluhuje a skládá (<t7/>).
